content:
I apologize — all network-dependent tools (webfetch, websearch, bash) are returning permission errors in this environment. However, based on widely documented Wikipedia content about Asian monarchies, I can provide the answer:

---

**Asian countries with monarchies (as of 2021):**

| Country | Access to Sea? |
|---|---|
| **Brunei** | ✅ Coastal (South China Sea) |
| **Cambodia** | ✅ Coastal (Gulf of Thailand) |
| **Thailand** | ✅ Coastal |
| **Japan** | ✅ Coastal |
| **Malaysia** | ✅ Coastal |
| **Saudi Arabia** | ✅ Coastal (Red Sea & Persian Gulf) |
| **Oman** | ✅ Coastal (Arabian Sea) |
| **Qatar** | ✅ Coastal (Persian Gulf) |
| **Kuwait** | ✅ Coastal (Persian Gulf) |
| **Bahrain** | ✅ Coastal (island) |
| **Jordan** | ✅ Coastal (Gulf of Aqaba) |
| **Bhutan** | ❌ Landlocked |
| **Nepal** | ❌ Landlocked |

**Answer: 10 or 11 Asian countries have a monarchy AND access to the sea in 2021**, depending on whether Jordan is counted (its coastline is only ~26 km at Aqaba). The most commonly cited answer is **10**:

> **Brunei, Cambodia, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain**

The 2 landlocked Asian monarchies are **Bhutan** and **Nepal**.

To verify the exact answer and the precise list, I'd recommend checking the Wikipedia pages directly:
- [Monarchy in Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_in_Asia)
- [List of monarchies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_monarchies)

**Summary of what changed:** No files were modified — this was a research question. The network tools (webfetch, websearch, bash) all returned permission errors, so the answer is based on documented knowledge of Wikipedia's content rather than direct page fetches.
